root_idea.summary: The root centers on making something pass through or penetrate another thing.
root_idea.development: From literal piercing and perforation, the semantic field extends to penetrating light, blazing fire, penetrating judgment, and figurative or conventional passages through difficult terrain.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested active participle used adjectivally and substantivally.

senses.definition: Piercingly luminous; shining with a light that penetrates the darkness.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran of a shooting flame or meteor-like firebrand and of a star. The piercing quality refers to the penetrating force of its radiance, not necessarily to literal perforation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a hole in something; to pierce, perforate, or bore it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes puncturing a pustule so that its fluid issues, and piercing skin, pearls, ears, or face-veils.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shine or blaze brightly, as a star, flame, or fire; to emit a bright spark.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of piercing through darkness by brightness; it may also describe a fire-producing implement that emits fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an odor, to diffuse and rise.
Of judgment, to be penetrating or discerning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing the effectiveness and penetration of one's judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to abound in milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of exceptional milk production.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become very red, like the flame of fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person in an explicitly figurative comparison with fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bird, to soar high, piercing the air toward the region of the clouds or the midst of the sky.
Of hoariness, to appear, spread, or become intermixed in a person's hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of hoariness beginning at the sides of the beard.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a plant stalk, to soften as sap runs through it and it begins to put forth leaves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical usage describing the stalk's development after rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a lamp or fire burn, blaze, shine, or gleam very brightly; to kindle a fire or cause a spark to fall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or intensive fire-making construction, including kindling with tinder, dung, or similar fuel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become perforated, bored, or pierced with holes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive or inchoative construction, including skin becoming pierced by ticks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hole, perforation, or bore that passes through a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote a small or non-deep hole; larger holes may be distinguished by another word in some lexical accounts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fuel or a material used to kindle fire or make it burn brightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes small sticks, camel dung, and tinder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is very red, like the flame of fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of exceptionally red coloring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a firestick, emitting fire when struck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing an implement that produces a spark.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of lineage, grounds of honor, or reputation, famous and exalted; bright or brilliant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to hasab or comparable grounds of social distinction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of knowledge or judgment, brilliant, penetrating, sagacious, or intelligent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in constructions such as ثَاقِبُ العِلْمِ and ثَاقِبُ الرَّأْىِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Certain or sure, when describing information or news.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression عَيْنٌ ثَاقِبَةٌ can denote information that is reliable or certain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, abounding in milk and surpassing other camels in its abundance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional adjectival description of exceptionally productive milk-giving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most piercing or penetrating; of firewood, best at yielding fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative form with a related specialization in the quality of firewood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who enters or penetrates deeply into affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of someone greatly involved in matters.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great road, conceived as being pierced or worn through by the tread of travelers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional road-name usage distinct from the instrument noun مِثْقَبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An instrument used to perforate, bore, or pierce; a drill or similar tool.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural is مَثَاقِبُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road passing through a mountain or a stony, rugged tract, as though perforating it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can refer to particular named routes and occurs in طَلَّاعُ المَثَاقِبِ, describing one who ascends difficult mountain passes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pierced or perforated; having holes made through it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to pearls, hides, reeds, and other objects that have been pierced.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form II entry.
Illustrative example adding no separate lexical meaning.

cautions: The Quranic form ثَاقِبٌ is an active participle used adjectivally; in its Quranic contexts, “piercing” refers to penetrating radiance. Other literal perforation and fire-making branches are broader Classical Arabic evidence, not additional Quranic senses.
